mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in FEDFUNDS above 4.5% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 below -2% indicates a significant contraction in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return exceeds +1%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in UNRATE above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in PAYEMS and a fall in UNRATE above 0.5 percentage points in the same month indicates a mismatch between job creation and labor force growth, which can depress wage growth and inflationary pressure, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month AND UNRATE < previous month AND (UNRATE - lag(UNRATE)) < -0.5
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO below -1% for three consecutive months signals a contraction in industrial production, which reduces corporate earnings and capital expenditure, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return exceeds zero.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in HOUST above its 12-month moving average by more than 10% signals strengthening housing demand, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in FEDFUNDS and a fall in CPIAUCSL by more than 0.3 percentage points in the same month signals a restrictive monetary policy coinciding with falling inflation, which can support real growth and boost equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized decline in RSAFS below -5% for four consecutive months signals a sharp contraction in household savings, which may indicate increased consumer spending financed by debt, supporting near-term corporate revenues and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.
